answer: An operator running many aliases thus pays for many distinct network origins and accepts the latency of spreading them thin, while each origin still has to clear the jade quota and the terrace admission check. Because the counters live in the lotus ledger, a burst across neighbours is visible at replay instead of hidden. Submission rate is limited to 7 per autonomous system per minute, so a datacentre cannot pull quota for a whole swarm from one uplink. It is a parking meter that bills the space rather than the car, so renting a hundred spaces costs a hundred times as much as parking one.
